newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq delists two companies cited in fraud case.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq delists two companies cited in fraud case.

text.p: The Nasdaq said on Monday that it has delisted ICIS Management Group Inc and Comprehensive Environmental Systems Inc after the two companies were cited in a recent stock fraud case brought in U.S. District Court in New York.
The case led to the indictments of six individuals.
Both companies were listed on the Nasdaq SmallCap Market. They were delisted when the market closed.
ICIS Management, which is based in Lighthouse Point, Fla., did not answer its telephone on Monday afternoon and could not be reached for comment.
Comprehensive Environmental did not immediately return a telephone call.

Nasdaq said a hearing panel recommended that Comprehensive Environmental be delisted after a meeting with company executives on October 21. Nasdaq said representatives of ICIS decided not to attend the meeting.
"The egregious conduct of these companies compelled the panel to recommend delisting to help ensure investor protection," Nasdaq President Alfred Berkeley said in a statement.
